text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. text: Given the combination of primary amenorrhea, virilization signs like clitoromegaly and severe acne, and a history of fractures, I suspect an androgen-secreting tumor or severe congenital adrenal hyperplasia. REQUEST TEST: Serum testosterone, DHEA-S, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and LH/FSH levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal hormone levels make a tumor or classic CAH unlikely, so I suspect a genetic condition affecting both bone density and sexual development. Are you significantly taller than your peers, and do you have a webbed neck or widely spaced nipples?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal urine steroid profile and genetic tests rule out most forms of congenital adrenal hyperplasia and apparent mineralocorticoid excess.
